**STOP — this round needs a B ruling on A-R327-REVIEW-SAME-TEXT-REMOUNT.** Everything else in round 327 is implemented and A's checks pass. The report is `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-327.md`, with evidence in `a-round-327/`.

**The STOP:** the code-reviewer found a small difference from HEAD, and I reproduced it in jsdom. It happens when a status update returns the same text during a fade drag and the next move keeps the same fade value: the status span remounts, so `aria-live` may read the same text a second time. HEAD keeps the node.
- **Severity:** the reviewer said Medium; I say Low. A user can only reach it if a source finishes loading during the drag (startup only) or with a second pointer.
- **Why it's not fixed:** every fix changes a ruled clause (§1.2.4 or §1.1).
- **Options for B:** (a) defer it as Low, or (b) have `previewStatus` skip the write when no preview is showing and the text equals the committed status. I tried (b) on a scratch copy only (then restored it): the repro stopped remounting and the 4 related test files stayed green (93 tests).

**What was done:**
- **Code:** B's sketch v3 applied cleanly on HEAD 234ccdd. The tree has the 11 granted files: 9 modified, 2 new.
- **New test DP16:** stopping playback mid-fade doesn't rewrite the readout. It also passes on a HEAD copy.
- **Docs:** doc 232 rewritten (l.4 exact, 7 headings in order, only existing test ids cited). Doc 168 has one stage-b paragraph.

**Checks I ran:**
- **Claims:** before editing, output equal to planning. After, only K2, K10 (`120 18`, above the ≥112/17 minimum), K13 and K18 differ, all as allowed. Re-run after my last edit.
- **typecheck / lint:** both rc 0. Biome still reports 15 warnings in the three folders. The scoped check on owned files is clean.
- **Unit tests:** 236/236 across the 13 files. The slowest is 819 ms, well under 50 % of the 5000 ms default timeout.
- **Mutants (on a scratch copy):** B's 7 are red on their rows, and the restored file is green. My stop-effect mutant is red on DP16. My marker-row mutant stays green: keys are refused during a drag, so jsdom can't reach those reads.
- **Perf** (run alone, `failures` []):

| Fade row | HEAD | Now |
|---|---|---|
| components per move | 103.25 | 21.633 |
| components max | 105 | 22 |
| move restarts while playing | 0 | 0 |
| stopped release commits | 1 | 2 |

  Trim, move and range rows are identical to HEAD. I did not measure the second stopped release commit at 0 components myself; that number is from B's probe.

**Other reviewer findings:**
- **Async-lane render (reviewer: Medium):** not reproduced. A timer-based status write during a drag gives the same DOM changes on my tree and on HEAD. I've asked C to check it in the browser.
- **Two Lows:** left alone because their clauses are ruled.
- **Architecture note for B/root:** keep the code as it is for now. It proposes one later task: move the committed status into the same store, which would remove these findings by design.

**Not done by me:** every browser row (B-FADE-*, video fade, the export sha check and G327-AUTH) is C's. The backlog item is not complete: stage c remains.
